processing: A mixed baked-and-pan-fired green tea: three rounds of frying, three of rolling and four of baking, then a final shaping, eleven steps in all.
harvest_season: Spring, as is usual for maofeng greens; the tender bud-rich pickings are the desirable ones.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, evenly curled strips, tender green and glossy with silvery buds and visible down.
appearance_liquor: Faintly yellow with a clear green cast.
appearance_wet: Even whole buds and leaves, tender green and bright.
taste_profile: A clean, high, fresh aroma, followed by a full-flavoured yet brisk and pleasant cup.

brewing.notes: Downy strips can cloud the cup slightly, which is normal. Keep the water under a full boil and pour off completely between steeps.

vintage_note: A spring green of the kind normally sold from the current year's harvest and best drunk within a year. Check the origin on the label, since the name suggests Mount Emei while the documented tea comes from Ya'an.
description:
Here is a name that misleads. Emei Maofeng points you towards Mount Emei, but the documented tea comes from Fengming in Yucheng district, Ya'an, in the Mount Meng tea area. It was first called Fengming Maofeng and later renamed.

What sets it apart is the method, which alternates pan-frying, rolling and baking across eleven steps. The stated aim was to keep the strengths of baked greens while avoiding the weaknesses of pan-fired ones.

The result is a neat, curled, silvery-budded leaf with a high and fresh scent, and a cup that is brisk rather than soft. It works well in a glass, or in a gaiwan with water a little off the boil. Boiling water brings out its edge too quickly.

When buying, ask where it was made and which harvest it is from. Teas with Emei in the name are many, and they are not interchangeable.
history:
This is a recent creation rather than an old tribute tea. It is described as a newcomer among Mount Meng area teas, building on local methods with modern technique, though no firm founding date has been documented.

Fengming was a township of Yucheng district in Ya'an and no longer exists as a separate administrative unit. Its name survives in the tea's earlier title, Fengming Maofeng.
